newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asia shrugs off Fed rate hike, focus local.
newsitem.headline: Asia shrugs off Fed rate hike, focus local.

text.p: Asian stock markets on Wednesday shrugged off the U.S. Federal Reserve's widely-anticipated interest rate rise -- the first in two years -- to focus on domestic concerns.
The U.S. central bank said on Tuesday it was raising its key federal funds rate 1/4 percentage point to 5-1/2 percent to ensure steady economic growth in a low-inflationary environment.
"To a certain extent the rate hike was discounted," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities in Hong Kong.
He said the Hong Kong market was focused on what actions the government may take, if any, to cool the current frenzy in the property market.
The Hang Seng Index was off 26.92 points, or 0.21 percent, at 12,805.61 at lunchtime.

In Tokyo stocks were little changed from Tuesday's close, with weakness in the brokerage sector weighing on the market following Tuesday's raids by Japanese prosecutors and the country's securities watchdog on Nomura Securities.
"The Nomura issue undermined the overall market," said a trader at a second-tier securities house in Tokyo.
The 225-share Nikkei average was up 45.14 points, or 0.24 percent, to 18,484.75 after losing 0.10 percent earlier in the session.
Wall Street had turned lower on Tuesday following the Fed's announcement, and ended off 29 points, or 0.4 percent, at 6,876.
A powerful 100-point rally on Monday had carried over to Tuesday, but the enthusiasm for the rally waned as traders turned apprehensive about additional Fed rate increases.
The rise in interest rates by the Fed was the first since February 1995 and prompted U.S. commercial banks to raise their key prime lending rates to 8.50 percent from 8.25 percent.

Elsewhere in Asia, South Korean stocks, battered by recent financial scandals, turned higher on broad-based bargain-hunting spurred by sentiment the market had touched rock-bottom. The composite stock index was up 10.42 points, or 1.63 percent, at 649.32.
Bargain hunting also propelled Taiwan stocks higher, as traders defied a farm crisis and liquidity tightening measures by the central bank.
The benchmark stock index was 185.90 points, or 2.37 percent, higher at 8,029.33.
Taiwan stocks lost more than 600 points in the four previous sessions in response to a deadly hog disease that forced a halt to billions of dollars worth of pork exports.
Philippine stocks ended higher, with the main index up 19.02 points, or 0.59 percent, at 3,223.14.
Malaysian stocks were off 0.23 points, or 0.02 percent, at 1,217.11, while Singapore's Straits Times index was down 1.74 or 0.08 percent at 2,098.21.
Indonesian shares added 3.01 points, or 0.46 percent, to 660.292, while Thai stocks were up 2.69 points, or 0.38 percent, at 713.37.
Australia's All Ordinaries Index was off 0.3 points or 0.01 percent, at 2,403.1, while New Zealand shares ended up 0.60 points, or 0.03 percent, at 2,220.87.
